Some Dynamical Systems in you

• All of your daily voluntary actions, as well as involuntary
 actions of your heart, pancreas, neurons, etc…. They’re all
 dynamical systems
• Their elements could be as big as organs or parts theorof
 downright to cells, and chemicals in them… Biology,
 Chemistry, and Physics are all about dynamical systems.
• So your speech system is a very complex dynamical system.
• Since there are so many dynamical systems, we can use one
 dynamical system to study another, due to the underlying
  similarity, despite extreme difference (We’re going up
 Diotima’s ladder!)

SGD starts with
a wild guess

What’s the average—the
 essence—of:
 [78, 67, 98, 85, 76, 68, 98,
 72]
 Pick any random number x
 as the estimate.
At time 0:
 x[0] = 130
Learning rate γ = 25%

One
observation
creates error
Randomly pick one number
d from the data.
 d[0] = 98
 Current estimate: x[0] = 130
Discrepancy / Loss:
130 − 98 = 32
The average should be close
 to the data.

Move 25% of
the error

Random observation: d[0]
= 98
Discrepancy / Loss:
130 − 98 = 32
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[1] = 130 − 0.25(32)
= 122
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[1]
= 85
Discrepancy / Loss:
122 − 85 = 37
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[2] = 122 − 0.25(37)
= 112.75
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[2]
= 76
Discrepancy / Loss:
 112.75 − 76 = 36.75
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[3] = 112.75 − 0.25(36.75)
= 103.563
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[3]
= 68
Discrepancy / Loss:
103.563 − 68 = 35.563
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[4] = 103.563 −
 0.25(35.563)
= 94.672
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

A high datum
pulls x upward

Random observation: d[4]
= 98
Discrepancy / Loss:
 94.672 − 98 = -3.328
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[5] = 94.672 − 0.25(-3.328)
= 95.504
A negative discrepancy makes
 subtraction move x upward.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[5]
= 72
Discrepancy / Loss:
 95.504 − 72 = 23.504
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[6] = 95.504 − 0.25(23.504)
= 89.628
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[6]
= 78
Discrepancy / Loss:
 89.628 − 78 = 11.628
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[7] = 89.628 − 0.25(11.628)
= 86.721
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[7]
= 67
Discrepancy / Loss:
 86.721 − 67 = 19.721
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[8] = 86.721 − 0.25(19.721)
= 81.791
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

A high datum
pulls x upward

Random observation: d[8]
= 98
Discrepancy / Loss:
 81.791 − 98 = -16.209
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[9] = 81.791 − 0.25(-16.209)
= 85.843
A negative discrepancy makes
 subtraction move x upward.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[9]
= 85
Discrepancy / Loss:
 85.843 − 85 = 0.843
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[10] = 85.843 − 0.25(0.843)
= 85.632
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[10]
= 76
Discrepancy / Loss:
 85.632 − 76 = 9.632
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[11] = 85.632 − 0.25(9.632)
= 83.224
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

Repeat the
correction

Random observation: d[11]
= 68
Discrepancy / Loss:
 83.224 − 68 = 15.224
 Subtract 25% of that
 discrepancy:
 x[12] = 83.224 −
 0.25(15.224)
= 79.418
The estimate moves toward
 this observation.

That is SGD

 1) Make an initial estimate
 / guess.
 2) Use data to improve the

mistake

 80.
The discrepancy shrinks.

toward 0.
